newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil soybean crop 15 pct harvested - Safras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil soybean crop 15 pct harvested - Safras.

text.p: Around 15 percent of Brazil's expected soybean crop had been harvested by March 6, consultants Safras e Mercado said in a weekly report.
The 15 percent compares with seven percent by March 7, 1996, and an historical average over the past five years of five percent, it added.
In the week ending March 6, weather conditions were good for the soybean crop and for the harvest, with showers maintaining soil moisture levels, Safras said.
A breakdown of percentage harvested by state follows.

PARANA - regular and fast harvesting. Average yields are around 2,650 kgs per hectare although in some areas it is exceeding 2,800 kgs per hectare. Total production seen between 6.79 million tonnes including a midcrop of 95,000 tonnes. RIO GRANDE DO SUL - harvest expected to begin in the second half of March in the north of the region. Yields expected to be around 2,000 kgs per hectare.

MATO GROSSO - good weather and use of fertilisers is leading to expectations of yields of 2,561 kgs per hectare which would be a new record for the state. GOIAS - harvesting a little slower in the past week due to rains in a large part of the southwest. MATO GROSSO DO SUL - north of the state a little dry and would welcome some rains. But production could still be higher than anticipated given well looked-after crops and reasonable climate.

SAO PAULO - good progress in the harvest except for the north Mogiana region which has been hit by rains. Still expecting however record yields. MINAS GERAIS - some rains slowing the harvest a little. But like Sao Paulo could still have record yields. -- Caroline Bulloch, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 5074151
